label: FSS (Alcoholic Beverages Standards) Regulations, 2018 — labelling
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
source_note: Encodes the Part-5 labelling provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages Standards Regulations, 2018. Generic declarations (name, net quantity, manufacturer, manufacture date) come from the Legal Metrology base pack; this pack overrides the base MRP declaration to respect the Rule 6(1)(e) proviso (State Excise Laws govern retail price for alcohol). The FSSAI food pack deliberately does NOT apply to this category, so veg/non-veg and nutrition-panel checks are not falsely raised. Statutory-warning and prohibited-claim wordings are quoted from the regulation. NOTE: this regulation contains no pregnancy or underage warning, and 'Strong' is a permitted beer class — none of these are flagged.

declarations.label: Retail sale price (State Excise governs for alcohol)
declarations.note: Overrides the base MRP declaration: for alcoholic beverages the State Excise Laws apply, which may not use the 'inclusive of all taxes' wording, so that specific format check is dropped here.

checks.message: A retail sale price is expected (State Excise Laws govern its exact form for alcohol).
Retail sale price is missing or is not a valid positive amount.
Alcohol content must be declared as per-cent abv (or as proof).
The statutory warning 'CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL IS INJURIOUS TO HEALTH' is missing.

declarations.label: Statutory warning — don't drink and drive

checks.message: The statutory warning 'BE SAFE - DON'T DRINK AND DRIVE' is missing.
The statutory warning must be printed at a size of not less than 3 mm.
An alcoholic beverage must not carry nutritional information on the label (Reg 5.5).
No health claim may be made on an alcoholic beverage (Reg 5.6).
A beverage above 0.5% abv must not use the words 'non-intoxicating' or similar (Reg 5.7).
Food containing alcohol must not be represented as a non-alcoholic confection or beverage (Reg 5.8).
Wine must indicate its origin (country or state).
Wine must declare the amount of sugar (or a recognised sweetness term).
Wine containing more than 10 mg/L sulphur dioxide must declare 'Contains sulphur dioxide' or 'Contains sulphite'.

reference_standards.label: Alcohol-content tolerance
reference_standards.note: The actual ethyl-alcohol content must be within ±0.3% (±0.5% for wines) up to 20% abv, and ±1.0% above 20% abv, of the declared value. Whether the declared abv is accurate cannot be verified from a photo — confirm by laboratory analysis.

reference_standards.label: Methanol, higher alcohols & metal-contaminant limits
reference_standards.note: Maximum limits for methanol, higher alcohols, aldehydes, esters and metal contaminants (lead, copper, arsenic, etc.) per beverage type. These are compositional/safety parameters, verifiable only by laboratory assay — not from the label.

reference_standards.label: Wine — non-veg logo for animal-origin fining agents
reference_standards.note: If egg white, isinglass or another animal-origin processing aid is used and residues remain, the wine must carry a non-vegetarian logo. Whether such an aid was used is a process fact not visible on the label — verify with the producer.
